clue.text: Transport article by iron vessel

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
A is the indefinite article
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A ship carrying goods is moved alongside an iron-hulled boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship after 'Transport', but here it is a container for wine or water.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass container for serving drinks, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Tea rose presented by composer

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a brier (briar) is a wild rose bush

explanation.surface: A cup of tea and a rose are handed to a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmanuel Chabrier was a 19th-century French composer, best known for the rhapsody España.
explanation.definitionFit: Chabrier wrote operas and orchestral works, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Spin doctor in contract to make a copy

indicators.note: the spin doctor sits inside the word for contract, so in marks one piece placed within another

parts.note: to contract is to shrink, reduce
a PRO is a public relations officer, the official title for a spin doctor

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is named in a contract so he can reproduce the message.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to duplicate it.

clue.text: Boring place to live

explanation.definitionFit: A dull speech is flat, and an apartment is a flat: one word for both senses.

clue.text: Press irritate oriental in rally

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze tight
to bore someone is to weary or annoy them
E is short for east, so oriental

explanation.surface: At a rally, an easterner pushes through and annoys everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press irritate' reads as a jumble, but each word is its own piece in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large gathering, especially of Scouts, so a rally.

clue.text: Animal worker to run away

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect
to elope is to run away to marry secretly

explanation.surface: A labourer decides to flee with an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift hoofed mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Darling nursemaid's family supports scholar, cause of an upset

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits below it, so the scholar comes first

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate scholar
Nana is the dog who acts as nursemaid to the Darling children in Peter Pan
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A beloved nanny's relatives fund a student, leading to an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like a term of endearment but is the family name in Peter Pan, whose nursemaid is the dog Nana.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on a discarded fruit peel is the classic comic tumble, so it causes a fall.

clue.text: Fish for char, to be cooked with no stuffing

indicators.note: the letter for no fills the rearranged letters as stuffing fills a bird
cooking a word mixes up its letters, so char is rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, so it stands for no or nothing

explanation.surface: A cook makes do with a char fish, prepared without any stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no stuffing' sounds like an unstuffed fish, but it means 'with O stuffed in': O goes inside RACH, the anagram of CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Northern resident produces energy to fly over Ohio

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed over another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to skim is to glide swiftly over a surface
O is an abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Someone from the north produces the energy to fly across Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eskimo is an Arctic people's member, so someone living in the far north.

clue.text: Dickens settled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to have lived somewhere is to have settled there

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens has settled up his bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' looks like the novelist, but it is the old exclamation 'what the dickens', where dickens means the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'what the dickens?', dickens is a euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: Placate primate hoarding vegetables

indicators.note: the primate stores the vegetables inside itself, so one word holds the other

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone calms down an ape that is hoarding its vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify them with concessions.

clue.text: A small fastening can alter one's course

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to change direction when sailing into the wind

explanation.surface: A tiny fastening can make a sailing boat change direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintack is a short tin-coated nail, a small fixing.

clue.text: Trick one out of a building

definitions.meaning: the chess piece is also called a castle, so it is one named after a building

explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to cheat, and the chess piece is also called a castle.

clue.text: Cloth worn by unfortunate in Kentish Town

indicators.note: the cloth is worn by the unfortunate, so it wraps round them

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton cloth
ill means unlucky, as in ill fortune

explanation.surface: A sick person in a London district wears gingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of London, but here 'Kentish' describes the town: Gillingham is a town in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillingham is a town on the Medway in Kent, so a town in that county.

clue.text: Possessed the time to be shown over the vault

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece over another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
to bound is to leap or vault

explanation.surface: Someone is possessed for a while when shown the vault.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound means held as if bewitched, as one possessed is held by a spirit.

clue.text: Crack concealed by key English motor-racing team

indicators.note: the crack is concealed by the two letters around it, so they enclose it

parts.note: E is a musical key
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A fissure is hidden by a key part of an English motor-racing team.
explanation.walkthrough: EQUIPE is French for team, used for a motor-racing or rallying team.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipe, borrowed from French, is a team, especially in motor sport.

clue.text: Evangelist having a drink about the situation

indicators.note: the drink goes around the situation, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: ale is a drink
a post is a job or position, a situation

explanation.surface: A preacher has a drink while thinking about his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul, the Apostle to the Gentiles, spread the gospel, so an apostle is an evangelist.

clue.text: Beat the difficulty in getting illumination

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Getting light shed on a problem helps beat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the light given out by a lamp, a kind of illumination.

clue.text: Water and ink spoiled clothing

indicators.note: spoiled letters are damaged and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Water and ink have ruined some clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is knitted garments such as jumpers and cardigans.

clue.text: Theatre performer eats teaspoonful of fish

indicators.note: the performer eats the teaspoonful, taking it inside

parts.note: a surgeon performs operations in an operating theatre
t is the cookery abbreviation for teaspoon

explanation.surface: An actor swallows a spoonful of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre performer' suggests an actor; it is a surgeon in the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish whose roe is caviar.

clue.text: Fine leg's disposition creates a sensation

indicators.note: disposition here means arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at fine leg is placed so as to cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine leg is a fielding position in cricket behind the batsman on the leg side; 'disposition' reads as temperament but means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is a physical perception, a sensation such as warmth.

clue.text: Destiny of king is fulfilled

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess
taken as written
met, as in met a demand, means fulfilled

explanation.surface: The king's destiny is realised.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet, from Turkish, means fate.

clue.text: Bungling bosses continually fill the mind

indicators.note: bungling means making a mess, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Incompetent managers are all anyone thinks about.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to preoccupy someone's thoughts constantly.

clue.text: Frank's idle boast

explanation.definitionFit: A blunt manner is bluff, and an empty threat is a bluff.

clue.text: Winger is an Oxford player with courage

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A rugby winger is a plucky Oxford University player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a rugby wing, but it is anything with wings: here a large fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a blowfly, a winged insect.

clue.text: The Istanbul traffic police are somewhat extreme

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: The traffic police of Istanbul are rather heavy-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra means beyond the usual, as in an ultra-conservative view.

clue.text: To drink loudly, not quietly, is a stigma

indicators.note: not means the letter for quietly is left out of the word

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
p (piano) is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Noisy drinking is frowned on as a mark of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult or a stain on a reputation, a stigma.

clue.text: Quick card game

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means sudden, as in a ... decision

explanation.definitionFit: A hasty decision is a snap one, and children play the card game Snap.

clue.text: See hunt sabotaged and be filled with fervour

indicators.note: sabotaged words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch the hunt saboteurs at work and get carried away with zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to show eagerness and excitement.

clue.text: Connive to be great in the last part of the show

indicators.note: great is placed in the closing part of the show, inside it

parts.words: the last part of the show
parts.note: the finale is the closing section of a show
G is short for great, as in GB

explanation.surface: A plot to make the climax of the show magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: To finagle is to scheme or wangle by trickery.

clue.text: A type of fruit tree or evergreen

definitions.meaning: a fruit tree grown on a tall single stem
an enduringly popular song, one that never fades

explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners grow standards on a tall stem, and a song that stays popular is a standard.

clue.text: The issue is about a drug that's exactly right

indicators.note: the issue goes around the drug, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A son caught with drugs insists he is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British slang for precisely correct.
